# Zero in the upper left corner is undecidable for seven 3 × 3 integer matrices

No algorithm decides whether the semigroup generated by seven given $3 \times 3$ integer matrices contains a matrix with upper left entry $0$; already six of the generators can be fixed once and for all.

Use the [zero-in-the-upper-left-corner problem](zero-in-the-upper-left-corner-problem.md) for integer matrices.

**Theorem (Halava, Harju and Hirvensalo).** There is a semigroup $S$ generated by six fixed $3 \times 3$ integer matrices $M_2, \dots, M_7$ such that it is undecidable, for a given $M_1 \in \mathbb{Z}^{3 \times 3}$, whether $S$ contains a matrix $M$ with $(M_1 M)_{11} = 0$. In particular, it is undecidable whether a semigroup generated by seven $3 \times 3$ integer matrices contains a matrix $M$ with $M_{11} = 0$ (Theorem 8).

An earlier construction of Halava and Harju gives the same undecidability for $3 \times 3$ matrices with $14$ generators, and a refinement of it $8$.

## Proof depends on

None.

## Expansion

Words over a three-letter alphabet are encoded by an injective map $\sigma$ into the integers, and pairs of words $(u, v)$ by $3 \times 3$ integer matrices built from $3^{|u|}$, $3^{|v|}$, $\sigma(u)$ and $\sigma(v)$, so that products of matrices encode concatenations of pairs and a suitable entry of a product vanishes exactly when the two encoded words are equal. The proof reduces the Post correspondence problem restricted to Claus instances, whose undecidability for seven letters the source derives from a three-rule semi-Thue system with undecidable individual word problem (Matiyasevich and Sénizergues) through Claus's construction (Theorems 3, 5 and 6 of the source). Neither result has a page on main; a good expansion links both.
